b2-25.title: A new townhouse
b2-25.story: Anna's family has just moved into a new [[townhouse]] on the edge of Kyiv. The [[interior]] still smells of fresh paint, and most of the boxes are still closed. While Dad tightened a loose [[bolt]] on the kitchen door, Mama looked for the [[detergent]] so she could do the first load of laundry. Outside, workers were pouring [[cement]] for the new front steps. That evening the power suddenly went out, and Grandpa proudly brought out his old [[kerosene]] lamp. By its warm light, Dad found the problem on the electrical [[panel]] in the hallway and switched everything back on. Anna, meanwhile, already had a plan for the [[decor]] of her room. She covered one wall with a huge [[collage]] of photos from her school years. "Now it finally feels like home," she said.

b2-26.title: A day in the garden
b2-26.story: On Saturday, Anna and her grandmother drove to the [[garden center]] on the edge of town. Grandma wanted a [[jasmine]] bush because she loves how it smells on summer evenings. Anna chose a purple [[iris]] for the flower bed by the front door. At the checkout, Taras begged for a funny little [[gnome]] with a red hat, and Grandma couldn't say no. Back home, Grandpa mixed some [[compost]] into the soil before they planted everything. Then Taras turned on the [[sprinkler]] and screamed with joy when it soaked his shoes. Suddenly something green moved under the bushes: it was Max's [[iguana]], which had escaped from his yard next door. Max ran over, laughing, with a bouquet he had just bought from a [[florist]]. "Happy birthday, Grandma," he said, "and sorry about my pet!"

b2-27.title: Getting ready in the morning
b2-27.story: Anna's family has only one bathroom, so mornings are always a race. At seven, Dad was already inside, using his [[trimmer]] on his beard and humming loudly. When he finally came out, the whole hallway smelled of his [[aftershave]]. Anna had ten minutes for her [[skincare]] routine and a little [[highlighter]] for school photo day. In the kitchen, Mama was making coffee in the [[French press]]. She added [[stevia]] because she is trying to cut down on sugar. Taras grabbed his backpack, and Mama reminded him to take his hand [[sanitizer]]. Then everyone rushed out of the door at the same time. Halfway down the street, Anna realized she had left her keys on the bathroom shelf, but luckily Taras had his.

b2-28.title: Moving into a new apartment
b2-28.story: Max's sister Sofia finally moved into her own apartment, and Max came over to help. The kitchen had old [[linoleum]], but the living room had real oak [[parquet]] that shone in the sun. They carried in boxes, a sofa and a soft [[pouf]] that Sofia had bought online. Her tall [[ficus]] barely fit through the door, and a few leaves fell off on the stairs. Max put a tiny [[bonsai]], a gift from their grandmother, on the windowsill. Then Sofia spent an hour on the phone with her [[internet provider]], who promised to connect her by Friday. "Perfect timing," she said, "because on Saturday I'm having a [[house party]]." On Saturday, Anna arrived with flowers wrapped in [[cellophane]], and the place already felt like home.

b2-29.title: Family news on Sunday
b2-29.story: Every Sunday, Anna's family has a video call with her grandparents. This week Taras had the biggest news: he had become a [[boy scout]], and he proudly showed off his new uniform. Grandpa, now a busy [[pensioner]], said he had been a scout too when he was young. Then Dad shared his news: the roof had stopped leaking because he had finally called a [[professional]] instead of fixing it himself. Anna told them about a new girl in her class who comes from a musical [[background]] and plays three instruments. Max was visiting too, and Taras gave him a high five and shouted, "Nice one, [[bro]]!" Anna rolled her eyes, because her only [[sibling]] could be so loud sometimes. "[[Mama|mama]], can we eat now?" she asked, and everyone laughed.

b2-30.title: Talking about dating
b2-30.story: On Friday, Anna, Lisa and Ira met at their favorite café to talk about dating. Lisa had news: her [[ex]] had texted her again, asking to borrow money. "That's a huge [[red flag]]," Ira said. "He only ever talked about himself, like a real [[narcissist]]." Ira, always the [[optimist]], believed that Lisa's true [[love story]] was still ahead of her. She even pulled out her [[tarot]] cards and checked Lisa's sign in the [[zodiac]]. Anna laughed and said she trusted honest conversations more than the stars. Then Ira shared happy news: her cousin Dan, who is [[queer]], had met someone kind at an [[LGBT]] youth club. Before they left, Lisa asked if her new red dress was too [[sexy]] for the school dance. "No, it's lovely," her friends said, and Lisa smiled and blocked that boy's number for good.

b2-31.title: Checking in at the hotel
b2-31.story: Anna and her parents arrived at their hotel in London late on a rainy evening. The [[foyer]] was warm and bright, and a [[friendly]] woman at the front desk greeted them with a smile. "Good evening, [[madam]]," she said to Mama. "You booked one room with a [[king-size]] bed and one with a [[queen-size]] bed, right?" Dad nodded, glad that Anna would have her own room. Their rooms were at the end of a long, quiet [[corridor]] on the fifth floor. Anna's phone was almost dead, but her charger didn't fit the British socket. She went back downstairs and asked the [[concierge]], who lent her a power [[adapter]]. He even found a phone [[holder]] for the car Dad had rented for the next day. Anna fell asleep happy, with her phone charging on the nightstand.

b2-32.title: A holiday villa
b2-32.story: For their summer vacation, Max's family wanted something special. Sofia showed them a [[villa]] by the sea, but it was far too expensive. Max's mom preferred a wooden [[cottage]] near a lake, while Max dreamed of a beach [[bungalow]]. In the end, they found a small house with a [[jacuzzi]] on a sunny [[patio]] and a shady [[veranda]] at the back. Every afternoon, Max read in the [[hammock]] until he fell asleep. On the last day, his mom went to a nearby [[spa]] and had her first real [[massage]]. "Next year," she said, completely relaxed, "we are coming back to exactly the same place."
